items.fact: Nesterov: gradient at look-ahead theta - eta beta v; corrects before taking the step
Adaptive intuition: larger steps where small and consistent, smaller where large or volatile
AdaGrad: divide by sqrt cumulative sum; good for sparse; LR decays to nothing

items.fact: RMSProp: exponentially decaying average; fixes dying LR; good for online/non-stationary
AdaDelta: no global LR; running average of past updates; rarely used
Adam: RMSProp + momentum + bias correction formulas; theta update

items.fact: Newton's method H^-1 grad; fewer steps; O(n^2) memory, O(n^3) inversion; impractical
Quasi-Newton (L-BFGS) and Hessian-free variants exist; practical descendants are structured preconditioners
Schedulers set base LR over time; adaptive only rescale relative to it, so used together
items.where: Reading In one screen lead; section 7 intro

items.fact: High LR early to travel, low late to settle
Two questions: needs T in advance? what shape of decay?
Constant after warmup: flat; base case for decay-free; ends above annealed run
StepLR/MultiStepLR: multiply by gamma at milestones; needs T; ResNet era; fine for small supervised
ExponentialLR: eta0 gamma^t; no T; convex, fiddly, rarely competitive
Inverse sqrt (Noam): 1/sqrt(t) after warmup; original Transformer; concave, degrades gracefully if extended
items.where: Reading section 7 shapes table (with Eq. 3 and 6.99e-4 derived)

items.fact: Linear decay to zero: needs T; SFT/fine-tuning default (HF Trainer)
items.where: Reading section 7 shapes table (HF default 'linear' and 0 warmup quoted)

items.fact: CosineAnnealingLR: eta_max to eta_min over T; classic LLM pretraining: Kaplan, Chinchilla, Llama
Warmup + cosine: still the single most common recipe
SGDR warm restarts (arXiv 1608.03983, 45 min): cycles; snapshot ensembles and vision; absent from LLM pretraining

items.fact: OneCycleLR (arXiv 1708.07120, 45 min): ramp well above normal, anneal below start; short fine-tuning, fastai

items.fact: ReduceLROnPlateau: reactive; good for small supervised; bad for LLM (noisy evals, non-reproducible)
WSD/trapezoid (MiniCPM arXiv 2404.06395, 90 min): warmup, plateau, cooldown last ~10-20%; decay start chosen later; DeepSeek-V3, MiniCPM, ERNIE 4.5; the 2025-26 pretraining default

items.fact: WSM (arXiv 2507.17634, 45 min): constant forever, decay emulated by merging; 2025, Ant Group Ling team
Why warmup: Adam moment estimates from almost no data, wildly inaccurate, large updates; warmup keeps steps small until trustworthy

items.fact: Choosing: WSD if budget may change; warmup+cosine to ~10% if fixed; SFT linear/cosine to zero 3-5% warmup; small supervised ReduceLROnPlateau or MultiStep; none: schedule-free or WSM
items.where: Reading section 7 'Choosing one' (fixed-budget line updated to well below 10% / linear to zero per Bergsma et al.)

items.fact: WSD removed need for T but not decay; extending after decay means rollback
WSM: warmup then constant forever; checkpoints periodically; weighted merge of last n
Merge weights c_j equal per-step weights w_i = sum_{j>=i} c_j; inversion c_k=w_k, c_j=w_j-w_{j+1}, c_0=1-w_1
Mean averaging = linear decay, EMA = convex; cosine/1-sqrt constructible; optimiser-agnostic; no loop change
Empirical: 16.3B/1.4B-active MoE, 400B tokens off 10.2T constant checkpoint; beat WSD by ~1.3 points
items.where: Reading section 9 Results and Correction box (+1.28 best checkpoint, +1.18 matched, single runs, picked on test)

items.fact: Merge duration mattered more than interval or number; EMA weakest
Practical read: storage small; merge is cheap proxy for annealing now

corrections: Final-rate claim 'nearer zero can hurt downstream benchmarks': unconfirmed, contradicted by Bergsma et al. 2025; shown in a correction box
WSM '~1.3 points': +1.28 best-checkpoint, +1.18 matched (from the WSM paper page)
'WSD is the 2025-26 pretraining default': softened; GLM-4.5 chose cosine over WSD on benchmark evidence; Semenov et al. find cosine dominates for most optimisers
'Muon ~2x sample efficiency': kept as Moonshot's claim (52% of FLOPs) beside Wen et al.'s independent ~1.1x at 1.2B
'warmup + cosine to ~10% of peak' for fixed budgets: updated with Bergsma et al. (decay to zero) and Llama 3 (1%)
